cells.tense: Care is going out, growth is coming back, and nothing here is being forced.
cells.act: release it on purpose, not by losing it
cells.ask: Notice what you're still gripping past any use it has, and close it out on purpose this week. Not dropped or abandoned — ended, so the grip becomes a decision you made.
cells.core:
You're tending something, or someone, and it is growing at its own pace. The care isn't wearing you to the bone, and you aren't squeezing the thing you're helping. That's the difference between holding space and holding on, and the work itself tells you which one you're doing: attention one way, pressure the other.
What keeps this going is finishing with what's already finished. Somewhere in the care there's an outcome, a schedule, or another person's next move you're still carrying long after it stopped needing you. Release fits here not as loss but as the close of something complete — hands opening because there's nothing left to hold. Let one of those close, and see what room it leaves.
cells.sheetLine: You are tending without forcing it, and it is growing.
cells.place: Where you hold what must be borne

cells.tense: Tomorrow already has its fingers around the thing that is meant to grow at its own pace.
cells.act: take the next step with only enough light for that step
cells.ask: For the next thing you want to manage, see only as far as the step right here. Take it without arranging the ones after, and keep the later turns unhurried.
cells.core:
There's a future in your hands, and it has bent your care into control. You're arranging, protecting, watching for failure before it has a chance to happen. The tighter the hold on what's growing, the less green comes out. From outside it looks like devotion, and often it is — but the thing being tended can feel the hand on it, and the hand is running past where the thing has actually arrived.
What you've already lived through is real material. Draw on that when you imagine what comes next: see it a year out, turned out well, and keep that view as the light by which you walk. Then take the single step the light shows. Not the whole road — just this one, and the next when it comes into view.
cells.sheetLine: You are holding tomorrow instead of tending today.

cells.tense: There was a thing you wanted to bring along, and its door is already shut behind you.
cells.act: move toward the thing you actually want
cells.ask: Toward the direction whose loss would sting most, make one small visible move — a call, an hour, a page. That's the whole ask, and nothing has to come of it.
cells.core:
The care went quiet, and not because you stopped caring. The soil looks the same, the motions still happen, but nothing is coming up. What's left of the care goes into holding, and holding alone looks like independence from outside. It isn't; it's distance, and you've been standing in it a long while now.
An empty pot doesn't fill by being pushed. Start with direction rather than effort. Take up the aim whose loss would sting most, and let one small move point at it — a call, an hour, a page. No deadline on it. The pull does the watering; nothing has to be forced to grow, only faced and turned toward.

cells.tense: You did not sign up for these roles, and the room still calls you the one who tends.
cells.act: stop holding what no longer serves
cells.ask: Take a load you're carrying that wasn't handed to you, and set it down for a week. No announcement, no speech — somewhere else, and out of your arms.
cells.core:
Somewhere along the way, being the one who tends became what you are in this place. Other people lean, and you're the leaning post. From your side it feels like depletion; from theirs it looks like the arrangement. The care is doing its work. What went quiet is whether any of it was picked, because the role runs without your hand on the wheel.
The move here isn't grand. Take a single load you're carrying that no one handed you, and set it down for a week. Not thrown, not punished — put somewhere else and out of your arms. What stands without your shoulder under it stands by itself, and what falls was not yours to keep upright. Either way, you learn which it was.
cells.sheetLine: You've been holding things that were never yours.
cells.place: Where you hold what must be borne
